speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my clinic. I see you have a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; can you describe when you first noticed it and what it looks like?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. Based on your history of outdoor activities and sunbathing, along with the location of the lesion on your left dorsal hand, this is the most likely diagnosis. Given your age and risk factors, I recommend a skin biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and rule out squamous cell carcinoma.
